title: Supreme Court Seems Skeptical of Trump’s Tariffs

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the Supreme Court heard arguments in the biggest case of its term about whether the president has the authority to impose the highest tariffs the country has seen in
sentences.zh: 周三，最高法院就其本届任期内最大的一起案件进行了辩论，讨论总统是否有权征收该国一个世纪以来最高的关税。

sentences.en: a century.
sentences.zh: 一个世纪。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Adam Liptak explains why the court seemed like it might be willing to say no to this president.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事亚当·利普塔克将解释为什么法院似乎可能愿意对这位总统说不。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, November 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月6日，星期四。

sentences.en: Hi, Adam.
sentences.zh: 你好，亚当。

sentences.en: Hello, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 你好，雷切尔。

sentences.en: Thanks for being with us today.
sentences.zh: 感谢你今天接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: It was obviously a very busy day for the Supreme Court, which was taking up one of Trump's signature policies, tariffs.
sentences.zh: 显然，这对最高法院来说是非常忙碌的一天，他们正在审理特朗普的标志性政策之一：关税。

sentences.en: Just to start, can you walk us through what was at stake in this case?
sentences.zh: 首先，你能为我们梳理一下这个案件的关键点吗？

sentences.en: So this is easily the most closely watched case of the term.
sentences.zh: 这无疑是本届任期内最受关注的案件。

sentences.en: It involves President Trump's central signature initiative, tariffs.
sentences.zh: 它涉及特朗普总统的核心标志性倡议：关税。

sentences.en: And it's also the court's biggest confrontation yet with the scope of executive power in the second Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 这也是法院在特朗普第二任期内与行政权力范围之间最大的一次对抗。

sentences.en: And the question in the case was huge.
sentences.zh: 案件的核心问题非常重大。

sentences.en: It was whether or not Congress has authorized President Trump to pursue tariffs, which are his main lever in international relations.
sentences.zh: 即国会是否授权特朗普总统推行关税，这是他在国际关系中的主要筹码。

sentences.en: And he says protecting the nation's security.
sentences.zh: 而他声称这是为了保护国家安全。

sentences.en: And just to be really clear, Adam, why would the president not have the authority to impose tariffs?
sentences.zh: 亚当，为了更清楚一点，为什么总统会没有权力征收关税呢？

sentences.en: Article 1 of the Constitution, which lays out Congress's powers, is quite clear that the
sentences.zh: 宪法第一条明确规定了国会的权力，非常清楚地表明

sentences.en: power to tax and tariffs are a form of taxation and the power to regulate international commerce is for Congress.
sentences.zh: 征税权——关税是一种税收形式——以及监管国际贸易的权力属于国会。

sentences.en: And Congress can let the president have part of its authority.
sentences.zh: 国会可以将部分权力授予总统。

sentences.en: But this is a situation in which the Constitution is quite clear that Congress needs to authorize
sentences.zh: 但这种情况下的宪法非常明确，国会需要授权

sentences.en: this kind of activity, that this is not something the president can do without that authorization.
sentences.zh: 此类活动，如果没有这种授权，总统是不能擅自行动的。

sentences.en: But Trump obviously imposed tariffs in his first term.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普在第一任期内显然征收了关税。

sentences.en: So why was that allowed to stand?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么当时被允许了呢？

sentences.en: And yet these tariffs in the second term are being so contested?
sentences.zh: 而现在第二任期的这些关税却受到了如此激烈的质疑？

sentences.en: There are laws that allow the president to impose tariffs in limited situations, laws that specifically use the word tariffs and authorize the president to take action.
sentences.zh: 有一些法律允许总统在有限的情况下征收关税，这些法律明确使用了“关税”一词，并授权总统采取行动。

sentences.en: But those were limited actions in the first Trump term.
sentences.zh: 但在特朗普第一任期内，那些只是有限的行动。

sentences.en: In the second Trump term, President Trump announces that he is going to use tariffs in a much more aggressive, wide-ranging, global way.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普第二任期内，特朗普总统宣布他将以一种更激进、更广泛、全球性的方式使用关税。

sentences.en: And for that authority, he turned to a different statute, IEPA, the International Emergency Economic
sentences.zh: 为了获得这种权力，他转向了另一项法规，即1977年的《国际紧急经济

sentences.en: Powers Act of 1977.
sentences.zh: 权力法》（IEPA）。

sentences.en: And as the statute says, it's meant for emergencies.
sentences.zh: 正如该法规所述，它是为紧急情况准备的。

sentences.en: And remind us, Adam, what was the emergency that the president was claiming to justify these tariffs?
sentences.zh: 亚当，请提醒我们，总统声称为了证明这些关税合理而提出的紧急情况是什么？

sentences.en: The president identified two emergencies.
sentences.zh: 总统确定了两个紧急情况。

sentences.en: One, he says fentanyl is entering the country and he needs to take action against Mexico, Canada, and China.
sentences.zh: 第一，他说芬太尼正在进入该国，他需要对墨西哥、加拿大和中国采取行动。

sentences.en: And the other, he says, it's an emergency that we've had persistent trade deficits, and that requires tariffs against almost the entire globe.
sentences.zh: 第二，他说我们长期存在贸易逆差是一种紧急情况，这需要对几乎全球范围征收关税。

sentences.en: But a bunch of small businesses affected by the tariffs and several states took a different
sentences.zh: 但是，受关税影响的一批小企业和几个州持不同

sentences.en: view and said that the statute he invoked, this IEPA statute, did not authorize the tariffs that he wants to impose.
sentences.zh: 观点，并表示他援引的这项IEPA法规并未授权他想要征收的关税。

sentences.en: And they sued, and the cases they filed went to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 他们提起了诉讼，案件最终上诉到了最高法院。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about the arguments today.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来谈谈今天的辩论吧。

sentences.en: I listened to them also, and they were pretty expansive.
sentences.zh: 我也听了，内容非常广泛。

sentences.en: They stretched for almost three hours, and a lot of time was spent really digging into the statute that you mentioned, IEPA.
sentences.zh: 辩论持续了近三个小时，大部分时间都在深入研究你提到的那项法规，即IEPA。

sentences.en: So, where do you think we should begin?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为我们应该从哪里开始呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I think it probably makes sense to spend a minute with the statute, because it
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为花点时间研究这项法规是有意义的，因为它

sentences.en: does say that if there is a national emergency of the kind we were talking about, Rachel, the
sentences.zh: 确实规定，如果存在我们刚才讨论的那种国家紧急状态，雷切尔，

sentences.en: president may prescribe by means of instructions, licenses, or otherwise, and that it says a bunch of things he can do.
sentences.zh: 总统可以通过指示、许可或其他方式进行规定，并且它列举了一系列他可以做的事情。

sentences.en: Like, there's 15 verbs.
sentences.zh: 比如，有15个动词。

sentences.en: He can investigate.
sentences.zh: 他可以调查。

sentences.en: He can block.
sentences.zh: 他可以封锁。

sentences.en: He can regulate.
sentences.zh: 他可以监管。

sentences.en: He can nullify.
sentences.zh: 他可以废除。

sentences.en: He can void.
sentences.zh: 他可以撤销。

sentences.en: He can prohibit the importation or exportation of various goods.
sentences.zh: 他可以禁止各种商品的进出口。

sentences.en: But it doesn't include the word tariff or any similar word, duty, tax, imposed.
sentences.zh: 但它不包含“关税”一词或任何类似的词，如税费、税收、征收。

sentences.en: And it's an open question whether it authorizes the president to impose any tariffs, much less
sentences.zh: 而且，它是否授权总统征收任何关税，更不用说

sentences.en: the expansive, aggressive ones that he instituted at the beginning of his second term.
sentences.zh: 他在第二任期开始时实施的那些广泛、激进的关税，这还是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: We will hear argument this morning in case 24-12-87, learning resources versus Trump.
sentences.zh: 今天上午我们将审理24-12-87号案件，学习资源公司诉特朗普案。

sentences.en: So, when the court heard arguments,
sentences.zh: 那么，当法院听取辩论时，

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court, the administration's lawyer focused on two key words.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法庭请允许，政府律师关注了两个关键词。

sentences.en: The phrase regulate importation plainly embraces tariffs, which are among the most traditional and direct methods of regulating importation.
sentences.zh: “监管进出口”这一短语显然包含了关税，这是监管进出口最传统、最直接的方法之一。

sentences.en: This enormous string of verbs.
sentences.zh: 这一长串的动词。

sentences.en: He says what's important here is the president can regulate importation.
sentences.zh: 他说这里重要的是总统可以监管进出口。

sentences.en: The power to impose tariffs is a core application of the power to regulate foreign commerce, which is what the phrase regulate importation in IEBA naturally evokes.
sentences.zh: 征收关税的权力是监管对外贸易权力的核心应用，这正是IEPA中“监管进出口”这一短语自然唤起的含义。

sentences.en: And that's a central question for the justices.
sentences.zh: 这对大法官们来说是一个核心问题。

sentences.en: Do you get from regulation of importation to tariffs?
sentences.zh: 你能从“监管进出口”推导出“关税”吗？

sentences.en: Because the idea here being, the statute doesn't actually include explicit instructions that the president can tax or tariff.
sentences.zh: 因为这里的观点是，该法规实际上并没有包含总统可以征税或征收关税的明确指示。

sentences.en: So the government is making the argument that regulate includes the ability to tax and tariff.
sentences.zh: 所以政府的论点是，“监管”包含了征税和征收关税的能力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Mr. Cotiel?
sentences.zh: 科蒂尔先生？

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 谢谢首席大法官先生，法庭请允许。

sentences.en: The challengers say,
sentences.zh: 挑战者们说，

sentences.en: Hey, if that's true, it would give the president enormous power if you read regulate to include the power to tax.
sentences.zh: 嘿，如果这是真的，如果你把“监管”解读为包含征税权，那将赋予总统巨大的权力。

sentences.en: It's simply implausible that in enacting IEBA, Congress handed the president the power to
sentences.zh: 在制定IEPA时，国会将重组整个关税体系和美国经济的权力交给总统，

sentences.en: overhaul the entire tariff system and the American economy in the process, allowing him to set
sentences.zh: 让他可以设定……这简直是不可思议的。

sentences.en: That there are any number of ways in which the statute actually at issue in the case does not confer the power to impose tariffs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，本案所涉及的法规在很多方面都没有赋予征收关税的权力。

sentences.en: It's just not there, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，根本就没有这一条。

sentences.en: So, Adam, talk a little bit about how the justices drilled down into what the statute said.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，谈谈大法官们是如何深入研究法规内容的吧。

sentences.en: So it has a lot of verbs.
sentences.zh: 它有很多动词。

sentences.en: It has a lot of actions that can be taken under the statute.
sentences.zh: 根据该法规可以采取很多行动。

sentences.en: It just doesn't have the one you want.
sentences.zh: 只是没有你想要的那一个。

sentences.en: So part of the argument turns into a kind of grammar seminar.
sentences.zh: 所以部分辩论变成了一种语法研讨会。

sentences.en: The word license is used in IEBA.
sentences.zh: IEPA中使用了“许可”这个词。

sentences.en: It's not used as a verb.
sentences.zh: 它不是作为动词使用的。

sentences.en: It's used as a noun.
sentences.zh: 它是作为名词使用的。

sentences.en: Really trying to understand not so much what the purpose of the statute was, but just what the words mean.
sentences.zh: 他们真的不是在试图理解法规的目的，而只是在理解这些词的意思。

sentences.en: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, for instance, said...
sentences.zh: 例如，凯坦吉·布朗·杰克逊大法官说……

sentences.en: Other places where Congress wants that particular form of regulation to be used, they say impose duties.
sentences.zh: 在国会希望使用那种特定形式监管的其他地方，他们会说“征收关税”。

sentences.en: They say you can tax, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，总统先生，你可以征税。

sentences.en: Here they don't say that.
sentences.zh: 在这里他们没有这样说。

sentences.en: That Congress knows how to authorize tariffs.
sentences.zh: 国会知道如何授权关税。

sentences.en: Congress does that all the time.
sentences.zh: 国会经常这样做。

sentences.en: And you look at all the tariff statutes that Congress has passed.
sentences.zh: 看看国会通过的所有关税法规。

sentences.en: I mean, they use language about revenue raising, tariffs and duties and taxes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们使用了关于增加收入、关税、税费和税收的语言。

sentences.en: All the language that does not appear in the statute you rely on.
sentences.zh: 所有这些语言都没有出现在你所依赖的法规中。

sentences.en: Several justices make the point that the absence of the word tariffs or synonyms, duties, taxes, imposts, is significant.
sentences.zh: 几位大法官指出，缺少“关税”一词或其同义词（税费、税收、征收）意义重大。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It almost felt like the liberal justices were trying to speak the languages that we often hear from conservative justices, which is to stick to an extremely literal interpretation
sentences.zh: 感觉自由派大法官似乎在试图使用我们经常从保守派大法官那里听到的语言，即坚持对文本进行极其字面的解释。

sentences.en: of the text.
sentences.zh: 所以，自由派确实很乐意成为文本主义者和字面主义者。

sentences.en: So it's true that the liberals were quite happy to be textualists and literalists.
sentences.zh: 而保守派则面临一种选择。

sentences.en: And the conservatives kind of faced a choice.
sentences.zh: 如果他们走那条路，对政府来说是非常艰难的。

sentences.en: If they followed that road, that's a road that's quite rocky for the administration.
sentences.zh: 但他们很难摆脱这种方法，因为保守派之间确实存在广泛的共识，即文本主义，即法规的文字才是最重要的。

sentences.en: But it's quite hard for them to run away from that methodology because there's really broad
sentences.zh: 我们不会去考虑判决的后果是什么。

sentences.en: agreement among the conservatives that textualism, the words of the statute are what count.
sentences.zh: 我们只会看文字。

sentences.en: And we're not going to try to look at what the consequences of a decision are.
sentences.zh: 我可以问你一个问题吗？

sentences.en: We're just going to look at the words.
sentences.zh: 例如，本案的关键投票人艾米·科尼·巴雷特大法官问政府律师：

sentences.en: Can I just ask you a question?
sentences.zh: 你能指出法典中其他任何地方，或历史上任何其他时候，这个短语“监管进出口”被用来赋予征收关税的权力吗？

sentences.en: For instance, Justice Amy Coney Barrett, who's a key vote in this case, asks the government's lawyer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于监管进出口……

sentences.en: Can you point to any other place in the code or any other time in history where that phrase together, regulate importation, has been used to confer tariff-imposing authority?
sentences.zh: 你能给我举出国家历史上任何其他例子，说明征收关税的权力是由一项甚至没有提到关税的法规赋予的吗？

sentences.en: Well, as to regulate importation...
sentences.zh: 有任何闪烁其词吗？

sentences.en: Can you give me any other example ever in the history of the nation where the power to impose tariffs has been conferred by a statute that doesn't even mention tariffs?
sentences.zh: 我认为作为解释问题，我们的论点比这更进一步，因为如果你看看那段历史，授权的历史……

sentences.en: Any bobs and weaves?
sentences.zh: 你能直接回答大法官的问题吗？

sentences.en: And I think our argument goes a bit further than that as an interpretive matter because if you look at that history, the history of delegations...
sentences.zh: 自由派大法官索尼娅·索托马约尔知道这是一件好事，她应该站出来支持巴雷特大法官，她说：直接回答问题。

sentences.en: Could you just answer the justice's question?
sentences.zh: 巴雷特又回到了这个问题上。

sentences.en: A liberal justice, Sonia Sotomayor, knows that this is a good thing, that she should jump up and support Justice Barrett, says, just answer the question.
sentences.zh: 所以他们真的很在意法规的文字说了什么。

sentences.en: And Barrett returns to it.
sentences.zh: 即使对于最高法院来说，这似乎也是对特定词汇难以置信的细致解析。

sentences.en: So they really care about what the words of the statute say.
sentences.zh: 对于法院来说，在小案件中这并不罕见。

sentences.en: Even for the Supreme Court, this seemed like an unbelievably close parsing of specific words.
sentences.zh: 这正是他们所做的。

sentences.en: This is not unusual for the court in a minor case.
sentences.zh: 他们卷起袖子，试图理解法规实际传达的内容，这些词实际意味着什么。

sentences.en: This is exactly what they do.
sentences.zh: 不过，雷切尔，你说得对，对于一个重磅案件来说，似乎取决于这种细致的阅读，这确实很不寻常。

sentences.en: They roll up their sleeves and they try to understand what the statute actually conveys, what the words actually mean.
sentences.zh: 那么你认为为什么在这个案件中会发生这种情况？

sentences.en: It's pretty unusual, though, Rachel, you're right about this, for a blockbuster case to seem to turn on this kind of close reading.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，真正重大的最高法院案件涉及宪法，宪法是用一般性术语编写的，并且是无数先例的主题。

sentences.en: So why do you think that happened in this case?
sentences.zh: 他们在那里以不同的模式工作。

sentences.en: Most of the time, the really big Supreme Court cases involve the Constitution, which is written in general terms and which is the subject of endless precedence.
sentences.zh: 当他们处理法定案件时，即仅仅询问“法规的文字是否授权了特定的行动”时，

sentences.en: And they're working in a different kind of mode there.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能采取这种细致阅读的方法。

sentences.en: When they're working on a statutory case, one that simply asks, do the words of the statute authorize a given action?
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是一次法医式的练习。

sentences.en: They're much more likely to take this kind of close reading approach.
sentences.zh: 这不是言论自由。

sentences.en: So this is a real forensic exercise.
sentences.zh: 这不是平等保护。

sentences.en: It's not, you know, freedom of speech.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，1977年的国会做了什么？

sentences.en: It's not equal protection.
sentences.zh: 显然，大法官们花了很多时间解析几个特定词汇的含义。

sentences.en: It's like, what did Congress in 1977 do?
sentences.zh: 但有一件事他们没有花太多时间解析，我觉得有点意思，那就是芬太尼危机和贸易逆差是否真的构成了紧急情况。

sentences.en: So obviously, the justices spent a lot of time parsing the meaning of a few specific words.
sentences.zh: 这让你觉得也很有趣吗？

sentences.en: But one thing that they didn't spend a lot of time parsing, which I thought was kind of
sentences.zh: 是的，我对此感到惊讶。

sentences.en: interesting, was whether or not the fentanyl crisis and the trade deficits actually constituted an emergency.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为有一种倾向，即尊重总统对世界局势的判断，认为他比九个穿着法袍的人更有能力判断什么是紧急情况，什么不是。

sentences.en: Did that strike you as interesting also?
sentences.zh: 你是不是也觉得那很有趣？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was surprised by that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我对此感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: I do think that there's a tendency to defer to the president's judgments about the state of the world, that he's better situated than nine people in robes to figure out what is
sentences.zh: 我确实认为人们倾向于听从总统对世界局势的判断，认为他比那九位身穿法袍的人更有能力去判断什么是

sentences.en: an emergency or not.
sentences.zh: 紧急情况。

sentences.en: They also didn't much deal with another textual concept, because whatever he's authorized to do, it has to deal with the emergency.
sentences.zh: 他们也没有过多处理另一个文本概念，因为无论他被授权做什么，都必须与紧急情况有关。

sentences.en: And, you know, Rachel, it's really not clear that tariffs on Canada deals with the fentanyl crisis.
sentences.zh: 而且，瑞秋，你要知道，对加拿大征收关税是否能解决芬太尼危机，这一点确实不明确。

sentences.en: It's also not clear that what can look like capricious and mercurial impositions of tariffs and then unimposing them the next day deal with trade surpluses.
sentences.zh: 同样不明确的是，那些看起来反复无常、变幻莫测的关税征收与次日取消关税的做法，是否真的能解决贸易顺差问题。

sentences.en: So the court kind of gave that, spotted that to the president and focused on the question of, did this statute authorize tariffs?
sentences.zh: 所以法院算是把这一点让给了总统，并专注于这样一个问题：这项法规是否授权了关税？

sentences.en: Did it give him this tool?
sentences.zh: 它是否给了他这个工具？

sentences.en: But all of this was only one part of the argument.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些只是论点的一部分。

sentences.en: The justices also thought that some really significant hurdles stood in the way of President
sentences.zh: 大法官们还认为，总统面前确实存在一些重大障碍。

sentences.en: Trump.
sentences.zh: 特朗普。

sentences.en: Trump and some of the justices on the right side of the court were quite skeptical that the president could overcome those hurdles.
sentences.zh: 特朗普和法院右翼的一些大法官对总统能否克服这些障碍表示相当怀疑。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Lowe.
sentences.zh: 我是维娜·洛。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: So Adam, before the break, you told us that some of the justices were quite skeptical that the administration would be able to overcome some other major hurdles in order to keep
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，在休息之前，你告诉我们一些大法官相当怀疑政府是否有能力克服其他一些主要障碍，以维持

sentences.en: their tariff authority.
sentences.zh: 他们的关税权力。

sentences.en: Walk us through what those hurdles are.
sentences.zh: 请为我们梳理一下这些障碍是什么。

sentences.en: So the most significant one, and you're right to call it major, is the major questions doctrine, which is a kind of principle of statutory interpretation.
sentences.zh: 最显著的一个——你称之为“重大”是正确的——是“重大问题原则”，这是一种法定解释原则。

sentences.en: It has been around for a couple of decades, although it's really quite recent that the court has started to refer to it by name.
sentences.zh: 它已经存在了几十年，尽管法院开始按名称提及它其实是相当近期的事。

sentences.en: And what it says is that if the executive branch wants to do something really big, Congress has to authorize that really big move in plain, direct language.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是，如果行政部门想要做一些非常重大的事情，国会必须以清晰、直接的语言授权这种重大举措。

sentences.en: So we were talking in the first half, Rachel, about whether you could tease out of the words regulate importation, authorization of tariffs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在上半场讨论过，瑞秋，关于你是否能从“监管进口”这些词中推导出关税授权。

sentences.en: Even if you could, there's this separate hurdle that says, if we're talking about things of vast
sentences.zh: 即使你能，这里还有一个独立的障碍，即如果我们谈论的是具有巨大

sentences.en: economic consequence, the major questions doctrine kicks in, and you're required to, the executive
sentences.zh: 经济后果的事情，“重大问题原则”就会启动，你必须——行政

sentences.en: branch is required to show that Congress really meant it, that it wasn't a kind of inference from words in the statute that were 20 words apart.
sentences.zh: 部门必须证明国会确实是这个意思，而不是从法规中相隔20个词的词语中推断出来的。

sentences.en: Justice Scalia used to say, Congress doesn't hide elephants in mouse holes.
sentences.zh: 斯卡利亚大法官过去常说，国会不会把大象藏在老鼠洞里。

sentences.en: It needs to say so directly.
sentences.zh: 它需要直接说明。

sentences.en: In other words, even if the justices ruled that the word regulate includes tariff authority,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，即使大法官们裁定“监管”一词包含关税权力，

sentences.en: there's this whole separate question of, did Congress actually tell the president that he could use this power?
sentences.zh: 这里还有一个完全独立的问题：国会真的告诉总统他可以使用这种权力了吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, if we were talking about a tariff for $20,000, about some perfectly routine thing, that's one thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我们讨论的是针对两万美元的关税，针对某种完全常规的事物，那是一回事。

sentences.en: But the major questions doctrine says, if it involves vast economic consequences, this different rule is triggered.
sentences.zh: 但“重大问题原则”规定，如果涉及巨大的经济后果，就会触发这种不同的规则。

sentences.en: And there's really no question but that these tariffs could hardly be bigger economically.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这些关税在经济上几乎不可能再大了。

sentences.en: Now, the Supreme Court used the major questions doctrine repeatedly to reject Biden administration initiatives on COVID, on student loans, and on climate change.
sentences.zh: 现在，最高法院多次使用“重大问题原则”来驳回拜登政府在新冠疫情、学生贷款和气候变化方面的倡议。

sentences.en: When the court rejected the Biden administration's student loan plan, they said, this is $400 billion.
sentences.zh: 当法院驳回拜登政府的学生贷款计划时，他们说，这是4000亿美元。

sentences.en: That's a staggering sum of money.
sentences.zh: 这是一个惊人的金额。

sentences.en: Well, the sums of money involved here, according to the administration, will easily go into the trillions.
sentences.zh: 好吧，据政府称，这里涉及的金额很容易达到数万亿。

sentences.en: And that sure would seem to suggest that the major questions doctrine plays a role here.
sentences.zh: 这确实似乎表明“重大问题原则”在这里发挥了作用。

sentences.en: Counsel, some time ago, you dismissed the applicability of the major questions doctrine.
sentences.zh: 律师，不久前，你驳回了“重大问题原则”的适用性。

sentences.en: And I want you to explain that a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我想请你再多解释一下。

sentences.en: So Chief Justice Roberts invokes the major questions doctrine directly, early in the argument.
sentences.zh: 所以罗伯茨首席大法官在辩论初期就直接援引了“重大问题原则”。

sentences.en: You have a claim source, an IEPA, that had never before been used to justify tariffs.
sentences.zh: 你有一个索赔来源，即《国际紧急经济权力法》（IEPA），它以前从未被用来证明关税的合理性。

sentences.en: No one has argued that it does until this particular case.
sentences.zh: 直到这个特定案件之前，没有人争辩过它有此功能。

sentences.en: And he asked the government's lawyer how it can be that a statute that doesn't name tariffs, that's
sentences.zh: 他问政府律师，一部既没有提到关税、在其50年历史中

sentences.en: never been used in its 50-year history to justify tariffs, and that's being used for a power
sentences.zh: 从未被用来证明关税合理，且被用来赋予一种

sentences.en: to impose tariffs on any product from any country for any length of time, satisfies the major questions doctrine.
sentences.zh: 对任何国家的任何产品在任何时间内征收关税的权力的法规，怎么能满足“重大问题原则”呢？

sentences.en: The justification is being used for a power to impose tariffs on any product from any country for in any amount for any length of time.
sentences.zh: 这种辩护被用来赋予一种权力，即对任何国家的任何产品在任何金额下、在任何时间内征收关税。

sentences.en: That seems like I'm not suggesting it's not there, but it does seem like that's major authority.
sentences.zh: 这看起来——我不是说它不存在，但这看起来确实是重大权力。

sentences.en: And the basis for the claim seems to be a misfit.
sentences.zh: 而且该主张的基础似乎并不匹配。

sentences.en: So why doesn't it apply again?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么它又不适用了呢？

sentences.en: And what does the government's lawyer say to that kind of questioning?
sentences.zh: 政府律师对这种质询是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Well, we agree that it's a major power, but it's in the context of a statute that is
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们同意这是一种重大权力，但它是在一部

sentences.en: explicitly conferring major powers.
sentences.zh: 明确赋予重大权力的法规背景下。

sentences.en: The government's lawyer says first, and not entirely persuasively, that IEPA is the kind of plain, direct language that you need to satisfy the major questions doctrine.
sentences.zh: 政府律师首先说——而且并不完全令人信服——IEPA就是满足“重大问题原则”所需的那种清晰、直接的语言。

sentences.en: But his backup argument is his better one, probably.
sentences.zh: 但他的备选论点可能是更好的一个。

sentences.en: He says...
sentences.zh: 他说……

sentences.en: As to that point, I believe the court has never applied the major questions doctrine.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我相信法院从未应用过“重大问题原则”。

sentences.en: The court has never applied the major questions doctrine in the foreign policy context.
sentences.zh: 法院从未在外交政策背景下应用过“重大问题原则”。

sentences.en: Why would it be the case that foreign affairs would be exempt from the major questions doctrine?
sentences.zh: 为什么外交事务会免于“重大问题原则”的约束呢？

sentences.en: The idea would be that domestic taxation is for Congress.
sentences.zh: 其理念是国内税收属于国会。

sentences.en: And if Congress wants to delegate some of its authority, perhaps it can.
sentences.zh: 如果国会想下放部分权力，也许可以。

sentences.en: But the president takes the leading role in diplomacy and as commander-in-chief in looking after national security.
sentences.zh: 但总统在外交和作为三军统帅负责国家安全方面起主导作用。

sentences.en: So the theory is that the Constitution gives Congress power in one setting and gives the president substantial power in the other setting.
sentences.zh: 所以理论是，宪法在一种情况下赋予国会权力，而在另一种情况下赋予总统实质性权力。

sentences.en: And so I guess in this case, the question then becomes, do tariffs actually count as foreign policy, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我想在这个案件中，问题就变成了：关税真的算外交政策吗，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: We have never applied it to foreign affairs, but this is a tariff.
sentences.zh: 我们从未将其应用于外交事务，但这是一种关税。

sentences.en: This is a tax.
sentences.zh: 这是一种税。

sentences.en: Justice Sotomayor says it's true we've never applied it to foreign affairs, but this is not foreign.
sentences.zh: 索托马约尔大法官说，诚然我们从未将其应用于外交事务，但这并非外交。

sentences.en: This is a tariff.
sentences.zh: 这是一种关税。

sentences.en: This is a tax.
sentences.zh: 这是一种税。

sentences.en: I just don't understand this argument.
sentences.zh: 我只是不明白这个论点。

sentences.en: It's not an article.
sentences.zh: 它不是一项条款。

sentences.en: It's a congressional power, not a presidential power to tax.
sentences.zh: 这是国会的征税权，而不是总统的征税权。

sentences.en: And you want to say tariffs are not taxes, but that's exactly what they are.
sentences.zh: 你想说关税不是税，但它们恰恰就是税。

sentences.en: The Solicitor General, arguing for the administration, says no.
sentences.zh: 代表政府辩论的总检察长说不。

sentences.en: It is a, if I may, it's a foreign-facing regulation of foreign commerce.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，这是一种面向外国的对外贸易监管。

sentences.en: That's a regulatory tariff.
sentences.zh: 那是一种监管性关税。

sentences.en: Commerce, everything.
sentences.zh: 商业，一切皆是。

sentences.en: This does seem to raise a genuinely interesting question, which is whether tariffs are domestic policy or foreign policy, right?
sentences.zh: 这确实提出了一个真正有趣的问题，即关税到底是国内政策还是外交政策，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, is it kind of hard to disentangle a distinction between the two?
sentences.zh: 就像，很难理清两者之间的区别吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it sure seems to be some of each.
sentences.zh: 是的，看起来确实两者兼有。

sentences.en: These are domestic businesses paying domestic taxes, largely in aid of trying to bring manufacturing back to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这些是国内企业在缴纳国内税，主要目的是为了帮助将制造业带回美国。

sentences.en: But, of course, they're also part of the president's diplomatic negotiations to try to address a drug crisis and a foreign balance of trade.
sentences.zh: 但当然，它们也是总统外交谈判的一部分，旨在试图解决毒品危机和对外贸易平衡问题。

sentences.en: So it's some of each, right?
sentences.zh: 所以两者兼有，对吧？

sentences.en: And this distinction came up throughout the argument.
sentences.zh: 而且这种区别在整个辩论中都出现了。

sentences.en: If one of our major trading partners, for example, China, held a U.S.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我们主要的贸易伙伴之一，中国，扣押了一名美国

sentences.en: citizen hostage.
sentences.zh: 公民作为人质。

sentences.en: You had Justice Clarence Thomas asking a hypothetical question.
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯大法官提出了一个假设性问题。

sentences.en: What if China held a U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果中国扣押了一名美国

sentences.en: citizen hostage?
sentences.zh: 公民作为人质会怎样？

sentences.en: Could the president, short of embargoing or setting quotas,
sentences.zh: 总统能否在禁运或设定配额之外，

sentences.en: say the most effective way to gain leverage is to impose a tariff for the purpose of leveraging his position to recover our hostage?
sentences.zh: 说获得杠杆作用最有效的方法是征收关税，目的是利用他的地位来解救我们的人质？

sentences.en: And I think he meant for that to suggest that the president should have available to him all kinds of tools to execute important national security measures and protect American citizens.
sentences.zh: 我认为他的意思是暗示总统应该拥有各种工具来执行重要的国家安全措施并保护美国公民。

sentences.en: It seems worth noting, though, that tariffs does not really seem like something you would deploy to rescue a hostage, but go on.
sentences.zh: 不过值得注意的是，关税似乎并不是你用来解救人质的东西，但请继续。

sentences.en: I had the same idea, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 我有同样的想法，瑞秋。

sentences.en: Everyone wants the hostage out.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想让人质获释。

sentences.en: But I think there are things much more immediate than tariffs, which the president could use to achieve foreign policy goals.
sentences.zh: 但我认为有些事情比关税更直接，总统可以利用这些事情来实现外交政策目标。

sentences.en: But be that as it may,
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，

sentences.en: the question from Justice Thomas did indicate that at least some justices thought that it was important to empower the president to be assertive and nimble in protecting the nation's interests.
sentences.zh: 托马斯大法官的问题确实表明，至少有一些大法官认为，授权总统在保护国家利益方面表现得果断和灵活是很重要的。

sentences.en: Justice Gorsuch.
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇大法官。

sentences.en: General, just a few questions following up on the major questions discussions you've had.
sentences.zh: 将军，关于你们进行的“重大问题”讨论，我有几个后续问题。

sentences.en: And then Justice Gorsuch in an extended series of questions, and one in which he became quite forceful.
sentences.zh: 随后戈萨奇大法官进行了一系列深入的提问，其中他变得相当强硬。

sentences.en: So could Congress delegate to the president the power to regulate commerce with foreign nations as he sees fit?
sentences.zh: 那么国会能否将监管与外国贸易的权力下放给总统，让他自行决定？

sentences.en: To lay and collect duties as he sees fit?
sentences.zh: 让他自行决定征收和收取关税？

sentences.en: We don't assert that here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里不主张这一点。

sentences.en: That would be a much harder case now in 1790.
sentences.zh: 那在1790年将是一个更难处理的案件。

sentences.en: Isn't that the logic of your view, though?
sentences.zh: 但这难道不是你观点的逻辑吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so, because we're dealing with this.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为，因为我们正在处理这个问题。

sentences.en: Indicated deep skepticism that Congress can simply hand over to the president important legislative powers.
sentences.zh: 表明了对国会能否简单地将重要的立法权移交给总统的深切怀疑。

sentences.en: And if that's true, what would prohibit Congress from just abdicating all responsibility to regulate foreign commerce, for that matter, declare war, to the president?
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，有什么能阻止国会放弃监管对外贸易、甚至宣战的所有责任，转交给总统呢？

sentences.en: Gorsuch says, what if Congress decides tomorrow, we're tired of this legislating business.
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇说，如果国会明天决定，我们厌倦了这种立法工作。

sentences.en: We're just going to hand it all off to the president.
sentences.zh: 我们打算把一切都交给总统。

sentences.en: We'll let him declare war.
sentences.zh: 我们让他宣战。

sentences.en: We'll let him impose taxes.
sentences.zh: 我们让他征税。

sentences.en: That's what I'm struggling and waiting for.
sentences.zh: 这就是我正在挣扎并等待答案的地方。

sentences.en: What's the reason to accept the notion that Congress can hand off the power to declare war to the president?
sentences.zh: 有什么理由接受国会可以将宣战权移交给总统这一概念？

sentences.en: Well, we don't content that again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们再次声明，我们不主张这一点。

sentences.en: Well, you do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你确实主张了。

sentences.en: You say it's unreviewable.
sentences.zh: 你说它是不可审查的。

sentences.en: That is unacceptable, Justice Gorsuch said.
sentences.zh: 这是不可接受的，戈萨奇大法官说。

sentences.en: All right, so now you're admitting that there is some non-delegation principle at play here, and therefore...
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以现在你承认这里存在某种非授权原则，因此……

sentences.en: There's a legal concept called the non-delegation doctrine, which forbids the legislature from handing over unlimited legislative power to the president,
sentences.zh: 有一个法律概念叫做“非授权原则”，它禁止立法机关将无限的立法权移交给总统，

sentences.en: at least without very detailed guidance.
sentences.zh: 至少在没有非常详细的指导的情况下。

sentences.en: He's basically saying this is a slippery slope, right?
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说这是一个滑坡谬误，对吧？

sentences.en: Uh, he's absolutely saying that, and...
sentences.zh: 呃，他绝对是在说那个，而且……

sentences.en: You emphasize that Congress can always take back its powers.
sentences.zh: 你强调国会总是可以收回其权力。

sentences.en: You mentioned that a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 你提到了几次。

sentences.en: But don't we have a serious retrieval problem here, because...
sentences.zh: 但我们在这里没有严重的收回问题吗，因为……

sentences.en: He went on to say that there's a problem with that kind of turning over of legislative authority to the executive branch,
sentences.zh: 他继续说，这种将立法权移交给行政部门存在一个问题，

sentences.en: which is Congress can never get it back as a practical matter.
sentences.zh: 那就是在实际操作中，国会永远无法收回它。

sentences.en: That's the political process working.
sentences.zh: 那是政治进程在发挥作用。

sentences.en: Yeah, it takes a supermajority, a keep-o-proof majority to get it back.
sentences.zh: 是的，需要绝对多数，即足以推翻否决的多数才能收回。

sentences.en: Because you'd need new legislation that could overcome a presidential veto, and no president is going to give back such power once he or she has achieved it.
sentences.zh: 因为你需要新的立法来克服总统的否决，而且没有总统会在获得这种权力后将其交还。

sentences.en: The president's a one-way ratchet toward the gradual but continual accretion of power in the executive branch and away from the people's elected representatives.
sentences.zh: 总统是一个单向棘轮，导致权力在行政部门中逐渐但持续地积累，并远离人民选出的代表。

sentences.en: I disagree with that.
sentences.zh: 我不同意这一点。

sentences.en: And it seems to fit with the very broad conception the Trump administration has of the power it claims Congress has ceded to it.
sentences.zh: 而且这似乎符合特朗普政府对其声称国会已割让给它的权力的非常广泛的构想。

sentences.en: It would raise the same issues.
sentences.zh: 这会引发同样的问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thank you, Joe.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，乔。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: it feels worth pointing out that this conversation we're having about handing the executive branch power and whether this is a slippery slope is not happening in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 值得指出的是，我们正在进行的关于将权力移交给行政部门以及这是否是滑坡谬误的对话，并不是在真空中发生的。

sentences.en: It's happening at a time when the country is in the middle of a conversation, basically,
sentences.zh: 它发生在一个国家正处于一场对话中的时候，基本上，

sentences.en: about whether President Trump is seizing too much power in the executive branch in all different arenas.
sentences.zh: 关于特朗普总统是否在各个领域夺取了行政部门过多的权力。

sentences.en: And so I just wonder if you feel like this particular discussion is loaded or what kind of broader context you, Adam, are applying to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想知道你是否觉得这个特定的讨论是有偏见的，或者你，亚当，正在应用什么样的更广泛的背景？

sentences.en: I think those comments really did address the current situation where we're seeing a president who's trying to accrue maximal power.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些评论确实触及了当前的情况，我们看到一位总统正试图积累最大的权力。

sentences.en: And the justices live in the world.
sentences.zh: 法官们也生活在现实世界中。

sentences.en: They're aware of that.
sentences.zh: 他们对此心知肚明。

sentences.en: And Justice Gorsuch's comments really moved the discussion from the parsing of the statute and how to interpret the statute and whether the major question is doctrine,
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇大法官的评论确实将讨论重点从对法规的剖析、如何解读法规以及“重大问题原则”是否适用，

sentences.en: which is a doctrine of statutory interpretation, applied or not, to a constitutional question of the proper relationship between the two elected branches.
sentences.zh: 即一种法定解释原则，转移到了两个民选分支之间适当关系的宪法问题上。

sentences.en: And whether the court should tolerate either the president claiming or even Congress agreeing to give the president power that ought to be reserved to Congress.
sentences.zh: 以及法院是否应该容忍总统的主张，甚至容忍国会同意将本应属于国会的权力授予总统。

sentences.en: And for all those reasons, we ask the court to reverse both the decisions below.
sentences.zh: 基于所有这些原因，我们请求法院推翻下级法院的这两项裁决。

sentences.en: Thank you, counsel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，律师。

sentences.en: The case is submitted.
sentences.zh: 案件提交审理。

sentences.en: And I guess I'd say that if the administration has lost Neil Gorsuch, it may well have lost the case.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，如果政府失去了尼尔·戈萨奇的支持，那它很可能就输掉了这场官司。

sentences.en: That you've heard skeptical questions for sure from the chief justice, Justice Barrett, Justice Gorsuch.
sentences.zh: 你确实听到了首席大法官、巴雷特大法官和戈萨奇大法官提出的质疑。

sentences.en: The three liberal justices are sure to be voting against the administration.
sentences.zh: 三位自由派大法官肯定会投票反对政府。

sentences.en: And this case is complicated, has a lot of moving pieces, is a rare jump ball in an era where the court usually is quite predictable.
sentences.zh: 这个案子很复杂，涉及很多变数，在法院通常相当可预测的时代，这属于罕见的“跳球”局面。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, on the evidence of the oral argument, these tariffs, at least, may well not survive.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，从口头辩论的证据来看，这些关税至少很可能无法维持。

sentences.en: And when can we expect a decision in this case?
sentences.zh: 我们预计什么时候能看到这个案子的裁决？

sentences.en: The court has put this on a fast track.
sentences.zh: 法院已经将此案列入快速通道。

sentences.en: The administration has asked for really quick treatment.
sentences.zh: 政府要求进行非常迅速的处理。

sentences.en: They think even having this case pending makes it harder for them to negotiate with their foreign counterparts.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，即使让这个案子悬而未决，也会使他们更难与外国同行进行谈判。

sentences.en: So unlike most big cases, which don't come till June whenever they're argued, I think it's quite possible this case emerges in a month, six weeks,
sentences.zh: 所以，与大多数在辩论后要等到六月才出结果的大案不同，我认为这个案子很有可能在一个月或六周内就有结果，

sentences.en: quite fast by Supreme Court standards.
sentences.zh: 以最高法院的标准来看，这非常快。

sentences.en: As we said in the beginning of the conversation, President Trump's tariffs are kind of the signature of a second administration.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在对话开始时所说，特朗普总统的关税政策某种程度上是其第二任期的标志。

sentences.en: And so if the court did not rule in his favor, that feels like a hugely significant blow to his policy agenda.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果法院没有做出对他有利的裁决，那对他政策议程的打击将是巨大的。

sentences.en: And the timing of these oral arguments can't help but feel a bit notable,
sentences.zh: 而且这次口头辩论的时间点让人觉得有些不同寻常，

sentences.en: given that they came one day after the Democrats had blowouts up and down the ballots in all these different states.
sentences.zh: 考虑到它们发生的时间，正是在民主党在各州选票上全面大胜之后的一天。

sentences.en: And also, this is all coming in the midst of a record-breaking government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 此外，这一切都发生在政府创纪录停摆期间。

sentences.en: And so taken together, this week feels a little bit like a referendum on the president's agenda in some way.
sentences.zh: 综合来看，这周在某种程度上感觉像是对总统议程的一次公投。

sentences.en: I mean, I know that these are disconnected, but that's a bit how it feels this week.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我知道这两者之间没有直接联系，但本周的感觉确实如此。

sentences.en: At the Supreme Court, it did feel like a shift, an inflection point.
sentences.zh: 在最高法院，这确实感觉像是一个转变，一个转折点。

sentences.en: And so it's notable, two things are notable.
sentences.zh: 所以这很值得注意，有两点值得注意。

sentences.en: One, that Trump would take this as a real blow.
sentences.zh: 第一，特朗普会把这视为一次沉重打击。

sentences.en: He has said that a ruling against him would be a cataclysm.
sentences.zh: 他曾说，对他不利的裁决将是一场灾难。

sentences.en: It would destroy the nation.
sentences.zh: 那将摧毁这个国家。

sentences.en: He has used the most apocalyptic terms to describe what such a ruling would be like, even to the point that some people thought he was trying to intimidate the court.
sentences.zh: 他用了最末日般的词汇来描述这样的裁决会是什么样子，甚至有人认为他是在试图恐吓法院。

sentences.en: But two, and building off of that,
sentences.zh: 但第二点，基于此，

sentences.en: if this court, which has in recent months greenlit lots of Trump programs on an emergency basis, provisionally, temporarily, but nonetheless, all sorts of programs,
sentences.zh: 如果这个在近几个月以紧急、临时、但无论如何是各种方式为特朗普的许多计划开了绿灯的法院，

sentences.en: if it stands up to President Trump now, that will be a much more assertive image for the Supreme Court
sentences.zh: 现在能够挺身对抗特朗普总统，那将为最高法院树立一个更加坚定果敢的形象，

sentences.en: and the beginning of probably a real clash between the president and the court.
sentences.zh: 这也可能是总统与法院之间真正冲突的开始。

sentences.en: So we may be seeing, really, for the first time in the second term, the Supreme Court saying, hey, we're a branch of the government, too, and we have a role to play.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能真的会在第二任期内第一次看到最高法院站出来说：嘿，我们也是政府的一个分支，我们也有自己的作用。

sentences.en: And we are not going to accept, in every setting, the efforts of a president who seems committed to accruing as much power as he possibly can at the expense of the other branches.
sentences.zh: 我们不会在任何情况下都接受一位总统的努力，他似乎致力于以牺牲其他分支为代价，尽可能多地攫取权力。

sentences.en: Adam, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 亚当，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，瑞秋。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: The Trump administration announced on Wednesday that it would cut 10% of air traffic in 40 of the nation's busiest markets
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府周三宣布，将削减全国40个最繁忙市场中10%的空中交通，

sentences.en: in a move that analysts said would force airlines to cancel thousands of flights while the administration tries to force Democrats to end the government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 分析人士称，此举旨在迫使航空公司取消数千个航班，同时政府试图强迫民主党结束政府停摆。

sentences.en: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cancellations were an attempt to, quote, alleviate the pressure on air traffic controllers.
sentences.zh: 交通部长肖恩·达菲表示，这些取消航班的举措是试图“缓解空中交通管制员的压力”。

sentences.en: They've not been paid since mid-October.
sentences.zh: 他们自10月中旬以来一直没有领到工资。

sentences.en: Duffy said that the affected markets would be announced on Thursday and the cuts would go into effect on Friday.
sentences.zh: 达菲表示，受影响的市场名单将于周四公布，削减措施将于周五生效。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Eric Krupke, and Nina Feldman.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗伯·齐普科、埃里克·克鲁普克和尼娜·费尔德曼制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor with help from Lisa Chow.
sentences.zh: 由德文·泰勒编辑，丽莎·周提供协助。

sentences.en: Contains music by Marian Lozano and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽安·洛萨诺和丹·鲍威尔的音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 由艾丽莎·莫克斯利进行工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何地方收听。

sentences.en: We'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次见。
